newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds mixed, curve begins to steepen.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds mixed, curve begins to steepen.

text.p: Irish government bonds experienced mixed fortunes on Tuesday as the short end continued to forge ahead while long-dated bonds suffered some profit-taking, dealers said.
"A little selling was expected after the massive buying last week. The long-end looks a bit expensive at the moment. We have seen Irish bonds strengthen at the shorter end again," one said.
By 1520 GMT the 8.00 percent bond due 2000 had risen 20p from Monday's close to 106.50 to yield 6.05 percent while the 8.00 percent bond due 2006 had eased 20p to 107.10 to yield 6.86 percent.
"The spread is 120 over the German bund in the five-year area and 85 over the 10-year bunds," the dealer said.

On Monday the National Treasury Management Agency (NTMA) redeemed 71.4 million punts of the 8.5 percent bond due 1996 and 412.0 million of the variable rate bond due 1996 but did not announce a tap issue.
"The NTMA redemption meant that people who were short of stock came in for what was available and that gave the market a further boost," one dealer said.
In the U.S, the Treasury market made small gains after the September NAPM index came in weaker than expected at 51.7 versus August's 47.4.
Dealers said Irish credit growth and government borrowing data released later this week will be crucial for the domestic financial markets.
Economists polled by Reuters said they expected Exchequer Borrowing Requirement (EBR) data on Wednesday to show a budget surplus of up to 175 million Irish pounds.
